SEI's 10-K gives initial terms of 3-7 years for TRUST 3000 and 5-7 years for SEI Wealth Platform, so 7+ is only the upper bound, and the figures date from 2016. The Avaloq survey (45% call their systems outdated) is vendor-sponsored and reported secondhand by finews. Nothing shows re-keying or screen-scraping around the dominant installed systems at scale.

Goldman lists 'Difficult finding mainframe skill set' as a challenge for InvestOne, alongside ~$6M a year in mainframe cost and FIS eventually ending mainframe support. That is a generic mainframe-skills point, not specific to this category, and comes from one company. differentiator: This category is more legacy-locked than typical enterprise software at the bank, trust and fund-accounting core: a mainframe COBOL engine (InvestOne) still keeps the books for most mutual funds, and audited performance history is hard to migrate.
